explanation: Deforestation accelerates erosion and strips away organic topsoil.

subject: Science
question: Why is CNG (Compressed Natural Gas) preferred over diesel for public buses in crowded cities like Delhi?

options.B: CNG turns into water inside tanks
options.C: CNG burns much more cleanly, producing far less black soot and harmful exhaust fumes
options.D: CNG is a renewable forest product

explanation: Cleaner combustion makes CNG significantly better for urban air quality (though it is still a non-renewable fossil fuel).

subject: Science
question: Which natural resource is essential for making glass (from silica sand), cement (from limestone), and steel (from iron ore)?

options.C: Minerals and rocks from Earth’s crust

explanation: Mineral ores and industrial rocks are foundational raw materials for construction and manufacturing.

subject: Science
question: Why do we call soil a "living resource" rather than just crushed dead rock?

options.A: Healthy soil teems with earthworms, insects, plant roots, bacteria, and fungi that recycle dead matter into nutrients

explanation: Soil ecosystems depend on countless living organisms recycling organic matter.

subject: Science
question: Which everyday transport choice helps conserve non-renewable fossil fuels like petrol and diesel?

options.B: Driving alone in a large SUV for 200 metres
options.C: Leaving car engines idling at long red lights
options.D: Walking, cycling, carpooling, or using electric/public metro trains for daily commutes

explanation: Reducing unnecessary fossil-fuel consumption extends finite reserves and lowers air pollution.

subject: Science
question: Water is technically renewed by Earth’s natural water cycle, yet many cities face severe water shortages every summer. Explain this paradox.

options.C: Although total water cycles globally, rapid overuse, pollution of rivers/lakes, concrete paving (blocking recharge), and uneven seasonal rainfall deplete clean local freshwater faster than it is replenished
options.D: The water cycle stopped working in 2000

explanation: Even a renewable resource becomes scarce locally when consumption and pollution outpace natural recharge.

subject: Science
question: How does switching from coal-fired power plants to solar and wind power benefit BOTH resource conservation AND public health?

options.C: It preserves finite non-renewable coal reserves while cutting smoke and greenhouse gas emissions that cause respiratory illness and climate change
options.D: It stops the Sun from shining

explanation: Clean renewable energy addresses both finite-resource depletion and air-pollution health hazards.

subject: Science
question: Why does it take hundreds to thousands of years to replace just a few centimetres of fertile topsoil lost to erosion?

options.A: Weathering of solid rock by sun, wind, water, and biological activity is an extremely slow natural process
options.D: Soil forms in 2 minutes after rain

explanation: Because topsoil formation is so slow, conserving existing topsoil is critical for food security.

subject: Science
question: A student says: "Since air is 78% nitrogen and only 21% oxygen, humans must mainly breathe in nitrogen to release energy from food." Correct this misconception.

options.B: We inhale the whole air mixture, but our body cells use OXYGEN (21%) for respiration; nitrogen is exhaled unchanged (though soil bacteria convert nitrogen into nutrients plants need)

explanation: Nitrogen is vital for plant proteins via soil fixation, while oxygen drives cellular respiration.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following explains why coal and petroleum are called "buried sunshine"?

options.C: They formed from ancient plants and tiny marine organisms that originally captured solar energy through photosynthesis millions of years ago
options.D: The Sun is made of coal

explanation: The chemical energy stored in fossil fuels ultimately originated from ancient sunlight trapped by prehistoric life.

subject: Science
question: In Rajasthan’s arid districts, traditional *bawris* (stepwells) and *kunds* worked far better than open shallow ponds. Why?

options.C: Deep shaded stepwells reduced direct sunlight and wind exposure, minimising evaporation losses while storing clean monsoon water underground

explanation: Traditional Indian water-harvesting architecture was cleverly engineered to minimise evaporative loss in hot deserts.

subject: Science
question: Compare a wooden pencil with an aluminium ruler in terms of resource renewability.

options.C: Wood comes from trees (renewable if forests are sustainably replanted); aluminium comes from bauxite mineral ore (non-renewable, so recycling aluminium is vital)

explanation: Understanding resource origins guides sustainable forestry and metal recycling.

subject: Science
question: Why are fallen dry leaves in a forest NEVER "waste" that needs to be swept away and burned?

options.C: Decomposers (fungi, bacteria, earthworms) break fallen leaves down into rich humus that nourishes growing trees, whereas burning them wastes nutrients and pollutes air

explanation: Natural nutrient recycling keeps forest soils fertile without chemical fertilisers.

subject: Science
question: Which set of three items are ALL obtained from petroleum (crude oil)?

options.B: Petrol, diesel, and lubricating oil (plus plastics/asphalt)

explanation: Petroleum refineries separate crude oil into fuels, lubricants, wax, bitumen, and petrochemical feedstocks.

subject: Science
question: Why do solar panels on rooftops work best when tilted toward the Sun and kept free of thick dust layers?

options.D: Facing the Sun maximises incoming solar rays, and clean glass prevents dust from blocking sunlight from reaching the solar cells

explanation: Maximum light transmission directly determines electrical output from solar cells.

subject: Science
question: How does recycling paper (notebooks, newspapers, cardboard) directly help protect forests?

options.A: Every tonne of recycled paper reduces the number of trees that must be cut down for fresh wood pulp, while also saving water and energy
options.D: Paper is made from iron ore

explanation: Paper recycling closes the resource loop and eases pressure on forest ecosystems.

subject: Science
question: What is the main difference between "weathering" and "erosion" in soil science?

options.B: Weathering breaks down solid rock into smaller particles in place; erosion transports/carries those loosened soil particles away by wind or running water

explanation: Weathering builds soil slowly, while unchecked erosion strips topsoil away rapidly.

subject: Science
question: Why do coastal towns and hill stations often have cleaner air than dense industrial traffic corridors?

options.B: Fewer vehicle/factory emissions combined with natural wind dispersion and vegetation keep air pollutants low
options.C: Cars do not burn petrol in hills

explanation: Air quality depends on emission sources, wind circulation, and green cover.

subject: Science
question: Which mineral resource is essential for manufacturing electrical wires due to its excellent electrical conductivity?
explanation: Copper ore is a key non-renewable mineral mined for wiring and electronics.

subject: Science
question: Why should used cooking oil, paint, and harsh chemical cleaners NEVER be poured down household sinks or open drains?

options.A: They flow into rivers and seep into soil, contaminating freshwater ecosystems and groundwater supplies

explanation: Preventing chemical contamination is just as critical as saving water volume.

subject: Science
question: How do forests help regulate the water cycle and prevent both floods AND droughts?

options.D: Forest soil acts like a giant sponge—absorbing heavy monsoon rain to prevent flash floods, then slowly releasing groundwater to keep streams flowing in dry months

explanation: Healthy forest watersheds buffer hydrological extremes.

subject: Science
question: Which statement about renewable resources is scientifically ACCURATE?

options.A: Renewable resources like forests and groundwater can still be depleted if humans use them faster than nature can regenerate them
options.D: Renewable resources can never run out no matter how recklessly we waste them

explanation: Sustainable management is necessary even for renewable biological and water resources.

subject: Science
question: A school installs solar street lamps, rainwater harvesting pits, and compost bins for canteen vegetable peels. Which three natural resources is the school conserving or regenerating?

options.B: Fossil-fuel electricity (via solar), freshwater/groundwater (via rainwater harvesting), and fertile soil/humus (via composting)

explanation: Integrating solar, water harvesting, and composting creates a sustainable resource-conscious campus.

subject: Science
question:
Assertion (A): Petroleum and coal are classified as non-renewable natural resources.
Reason (R): Although they formed naturally from ancient living organisms, their formation takes millions of years—far slower than the rate at which humans consume them.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

explanation: Renewability is defined relative to human timescales; million-year formation makes fossil fuels effectively finite.

subject: Science
question:
Assertion (A): Cutting down all forests on a steep hillside increases the risk of landslides and muddy floods in the valley below.
Reason (R): Tree roots anchor hillside soil firmly and forest foliage slows down falling rainwater so it can soak into the ground gradually.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

explanation: Removing root reinforcement and canopy interception leaves steep slopes vulnerable to rapid erosion and landslides.

subject: Science
question: Case Study: A village relies on borewells for drinking water. Over 10 years, the groundwater level drops from 15 metres deep to 65 metres deep because farmers pump water nonstop and all monsoon rainwater drains away over newly paved roads. Which combination of actions will BEST restore the village’s water table?

options.A: Pave the remaining open pastures with concrete
options.B: Cut down all trees near the fields
options.C: Drill borewells 500 metres deeper without conservation
options.D: Build check dams, percolation tanks, and rooftop rainwater recharge pits, and shift to water-saving drip irrigation

explanation: Balancing recharge (check dams/rainwater harvesting) with demand reduction (drip irrigation) sustainably restores aquifers.

subject: Science
question: Why is switching a city’s electricity supply from coal to solar/wind energy MORE sustainable than switching from petrol cars to electric cars if the electricity still comes 100% from burning coal?

options.A: Coal produces zero pollution in power plants
options.B: Electric cars burn petrol inside batteries
options.D: Electric cars shift emissions from tailpipes to power stations; pairing electric mobility with renewable solar/wind electricity cuts fossil-fuel use across the entire chain

explanation: True sustainability evaluates the entire energy chain from generation to end use.

subject: Science
question:
A student tests three soil samples by pouring 100 mL of water through funnels packed with each sample:
• Sample X (sandy soil): 80 mL drains through in 1 minute
• Sample Y (loamy soil with humus): 45 mL drains through; stays moist and crumbly
• Sample Z (heavy clay soil): only 10 mL drains through; water pools on top
Which sample is generally BEST for growing most garden crops and why?

options.A: Sample X, because it holds no water
options.B: Sample Z, because waterlogged roots never need air
options.C: Sample Y (loamy soil with humus), because it balances good water retention with adequate drainage and air spaces for root respiration
options.D: None of them can grow plants

explanation: Loamy humus-rich soil provides optimal moisture, nutrients, and aeration simultaneously.

subject: Science
question: Why are smartphones and laptops considered a hidden drain on NON-RENEWABLE mineral resources, and what is the responsible solution?

options.A: Throwing phones in rivers cleans water
options.B: Circuit boards and batteries require mined metals (copper, lithium, cobalt, gold); repairing devices longer and recycling e-waste recovers these finite minerals
options.C: Phones are made purely from wood

explanation: E-waste recycling recovers valuable finite metals and prevents toxic leaching into soil and water.

subject: Science
question: During a sunny day, a forest absorbs carbon dioxide and releases oxygen. At night, trees stop photosynthesis and respire (releasing small amounts of CO2). Why is a forest STILL a net producer of oxygen and carbon sink over a full year?

options.D: The oxygen produced and carbon stored in growing wood/leaves during daytime photosynthesis far exceeds what the forest consumes during respiration

explanation: Growing biomass represents net carbon captured from the atmosphere and net oxygen released.

subject: Science
question: Why is wind energy NOT equally practical in every single location on Earth?

options.D: Wind turbines need sites with consistently strong, steady wind speeds (such as coasts, mountain passes, and open plains) to generate reliable electricity economically

explanation: Site selection based on meteorological wind data (like Anna Mani’s wind-mapping work) is crucial for wind farms.

subject: Science
question: Compare solar energy and wind energy: what major practical challenge do BOTH share, and how do engineers solve it?

options.C: Both are intermittent (no sun at night; wind can die down); engineers combine them with battery storage and diverse grid sources to ensure 24/7 power

explanation: Energy storage and hybrid renewable grids overcome natural intermittency of sun and wind.

subject: Science
question: A family replaces 10 old 60 W incandescent bulbs with 10 modern 9 W LED bulbs that give the same brightness. How much electrical power (in watts) do they save whenever all 10 bulbs are ON?
explanation: Old total = 10 × 60 = 600 W; New total = 10 × 9 = 90 W; Savings = 600 − 90 = 510 W.

subject: Science
question: Why did traditional Indian villages protect "sacred groves" (*Devrai*, *Orans*, *Kavu*) where cutting trees or hunting was strictly forbidden?

options.B: Cultural protection preserved patches of native biodiversity, medicinal plants, wildlife habitats, and local water springs across generations
options.D: Because trees there were made of stone

explanation: Sacred groves represent centuries-old community conservation systems protecting biodiversity and watersheds.

subject: Science
question: If a leaking tap drips 1 drop per second and wastes about 15 litres of clean water per day, approximately how many litres are wasted in a 30-day month?
explanation: 15 L/day × 30 days = 450 litres wasted from just one small leak!

subject: Science
question: Why is topsoil (the uppermost dark layer of soil) far more valuable for agriculture than the rocky subsoil metres below it?

options.A: Topsoil is made of pure sand
options.D: Topsoil contains the highest concentration of humus, essential plant nutrients, water-holding capacity, and beneficial soil microbes/earthworms

explanation: Losing the thin fertile topsoil layer drastically reduces crop yields.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following best describes "sustainable use" of natural resources?

options.A: Banning all use of water and sunlight
options.B: Using all coal and forests as fast as possible today
options.C: Meeting our present needs responsibly while conserving and regenerating resources so future generations can also meet their needs

explanation: Sustainability balances current human well-being with long-term ecological preservation.

subject: Science
question: Why does air pollution in cities often worsen sharply during calm, cold winter nights compared to windy summer afternoons?

options.B: Cars burn twice as much oxygen in winter
options.C: Cold still air traps smoke and vehicle exhaust near the ground (reducing dispersion), whereas summer wind and rising warm air carry pollutants away

explanation: Meteorological conditions like low wind and temperature inversions concentrate urban air pollutants.

subject: Science
question: A coastal city runs out of river water and builds a desalination plant to turn seawater into drinking water. Why is conserving natural freshwater STILL far preferable to relying solely on desalination?

options.B: Desalination requires huge amounts of energy, is expensive, and produces concentrated salty brine waste—making conservation and rainwater harvesting far cheaper and greener
options.D: Seawater has no water in it

explanation: Preventing waste and recharging natural freshwater is much more energy-efficient and eco-friendly than industrial desalination.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following is an example of how ancient Indian engineering worked in harmony with Nature’s Treasures?

options.B: Burning plastic waste in open pits
options.D: Stepwells (*bawris*), check dams (*johads*), and earthen pots (*matkas*) that harvested rain and cooled water using gravity and natural evaporation without electricity

explanation: Traditional ecological wisdom leveraged local climate, materials, and natural cycles sustainably.

subject: Science
question: Why is nitrogen—despite making up 78% of the air—NOT directly usable by most crop plants straight from the sky?

options.D: Plants cannot break nitrogen gas directly from air; special soil bacteria (like *Rhizobium* in legume roots) convert atmospheric nitrogen into soluble soil compounds plants can absorb

explanation: Biological nitrogen fixation links atmospheric nitrogen to fertile soil and healthy crops.

subject: Science
question: Case Study: A hilly region replaces its mixed native forest with a bare stone quarry and unpaved haul roads. Within two monsoons, villagers notice three linked changes: (1) local streams turn muddy brown during rain, (2) the streams dry up completely by February instead of flowing all year, and (3) farm yields in the valley drop. Explain the single root ecological chain connecting all three.

options.A: Deforestation removed canopy and root systems → heavy rain eroded nutrient-rich topsoil into streams (muddy water & lower farm fertility) AND ran off rapidly instead of recharging groundwater (streams drying up by February)
options.B: Fish drank all the stream water

explanation: Forests simultaneously anchor soil, preserve fertility, and regulate groundwater recharge.

subject: Science
question: A school with 500 students uses 20 litres of water per student per day (10,000 L/day). By installing push-tap aerators and fixing leaks, usage drops by 30%. How much water does the school save over a 200-day academic year?
explanation: Daily saving = 30% of 10,000 L = 3,000 L/day. Over 200 days: 3,000 × 200 = 600,000 litres!

subject: Science
question: Why is "Plant a monoculture of fast-growing non-native trees" NOT equivalent to conserving an existing natural forest?

options.A: Fast-growing trees do not perform photosynthesis
options.B: A natural forest is a complex, centuries-old ecosystem of diverse native trees, shrubs, fungi, soil microbes, birds, and animals that a single-species plantation cannot quickly replicate

explanation: Protecting intact native forests preserves irreplaceable biodiversity and ecological balance.

subject: Science
question:
Assertion (A): Even though the Sun is 150 million kilometres away, almost every renewable energy source on Earth—including solar, wind, and hydroelectric power—ultimately depends on solar energy.
Reason (R): Sunlight heats Earth unevenly to create wind, evaporates ocean water to power the rain-fed rivers behind hydro dams, and directly powers solar panels.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

explanation: Solar radiation drives atmospheric circulation (wind), the water cycle (hydropower), and photovoltaics.

subject: Science
question: A town generates 100% of its daytime electricity from rooftop solar panels. On a cloudy monsoon evening at 8 PM, the town still has bright lights and working fans. Which engineering component made this possible?

options.B: Solar panels working in total darkness
options.D: Energy storage (such as rechargeable battery banks) or grid connection that stores surplus daytime solar electricity for nighttime use

explanation: Battery storage bridges the gap between sunny daytime generation and nighttime electricity demand.

subject: Science
question: Why does burning a wooden log release carbon dioxide that was captured within the last few decades, whereas burning coal releases carbon that was locked underground for hundreds of millions of years?

options.D: Trees absorb CO2 during their recent lifetime (part of the active surface carbon cycle), whereas burning fossil coal adds ancient sequestered carbon back into today’s atmosphere, raising total atmospheric CO2

explanation: Releasing ancient fossilised carbon rapidly shifts Earth’s atmospheric balance and drives climate warming.

subject: Science
question: A student compares two villages: Village A burns crop stubble in open fields after harvest; Village B mixes chopped crop stubble back into the soil to decompose. After 5 years, how will their air quality and soil health differ?

options.A: Village B enjoys cleaner air and richer, humus-filled moisture-retaining soil, whereas Village A suffers toxic winter smog and declining soil organic matter
options.B: Both have identical soil and air
options.C: Village A has cleaner air and better humus

explanation: Returning organic crop residue to soil builds humus and eliminates severe stubble-burning air pollution.

subject: Science
question: If Earth’s atmosphere suddenly lost its 21% oxygen and became 100% nitrogen, which TWO everyday processes would stop immediately?

options.C: Respiration of animals/plants AND burning (combustion) of fuels

explanation: Oxygen is essential for both aerobic biological respiration and combustion.

subject: Science
question: A farmer wants to protect a newly ploughed sloping field from monsoon soil erosion. Which agricultural practice is MOST effective?

options.A: Flooding the slope with salty water
options.B: Ploughing straight up and down the slope so water races downhill
options.C: Removing all grass and trees around the field
options.D: Contour ploughing (ploughing across the slope) and planting grass/tree bunds along field edges to slow rainwater runoff

explanation: Slowing runoff across slopes traps topsoil and increases water infiltration.

subject: Science
question: Why is groundwater in coastal towns sometimes ruined by "saltwater intrusion" when people pump borewells excessively?

options.B: Lowering the underground freshwater table below sea level allows salty ocean water to seep inland into the emptied coastal aquifers

explanation: Over-extraction near coasts pulls saline seawater into freshwater aquifers, ruining drinking wells.

subject: Science
question: Case Study: India has expanded solar parks dramatically in Rajasthan (like Bhadla Solar Park) while also expanding wind parks in Tamil Nadu and Gujarat. Why is combining geographical regions and multiple renewable sources a smart national strategy?

options.A: Wind turbines only work in winter
options.B: Different regions peak in different seasons (e.g., strong monsoon winds when skies are cloudy, bright winter/summer sun when winds are calmer), creating a steadier year-round clean energy supply
options.C: Solar panels only work in deserts
options.D: Rajasthan has no wind and Tamil Nadu has no sun

explanation: Geographic and technological diversity smooths out seasonal fluctuations in renewable generation.

subject: Science
question: Which 3R hierarchy (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) places actions in order from MOST effective to LEAST effective for conserving natural resources?

options.A: Recycle first → Buy extra → Throw away
options.B: Reduce consumption first → Reuse items as they are → Recycle materials when they can no longer be reused

explanation: Avoiding unnecessary extraction (Reduce) saves the most energy and resources; Reuse avoids reprocessing; Recycle recovers raw materials.

subject: Science
question: Why is composting kitchen vegetable peels and dry garden leaves superior to dumping them into a mixed plastic landfill?

options.B: Peels turn into plastic in landfills
options.D: Composting aerobically recycles organic nutrients into fertile humus for gardens, whereas burying wet waste in landfills wastes nutrients and emits methane gas

explanation: Source segregation and composting return biological nutrients safely to soil.

subject: Science
question: A limestone quarry supplies raw material for cement, an iron mine supplies ore for steel, and a bauxite mine supplies ore for aluminium. What do ALL THREE industries have in common regarding resource classification?

options.B: All three are renewable within one year
options.C: All three rely on non-renewable mineral resources from Earth’s crust, requiring efficient design, minimal waste, and recycling

explanation: Mineral ores are finite geological treasures that must be used judiciously and recycled.

subject: Science
question: Why do wetlands (marshes, lakes, and floodplains) deserve protection as "Nature’s Treasures" alongside forests?

options.C: Wetlands absorb floodwaters, recharge groundwater, filter pollutants naturally, and shelter rich aquatic biodiversity and migratory birds

explanation: Wetlands act as natural kidneys and flood sponges in regional watersheds.

subject: Science
question: A town switches 2,000 diesel-powered irrigation pumps to solar-powered water pumps. While this saves huge amounts of diesel and cuts air pollution, what NEW resource-management risk must farmers still watch out for?

options.A: Because solar electricity feels "free" once installed, farmers must avoid over-pumping groundwater and should pair solar pumps with drip irrigation

explanation: Solving one resource problem (fossil fuel) still requires responsible stewardship of another (groundwater).

subject: Science
question: Why is clean air considered a shared "common treasure" that cannot be protected by just one household acting alone?

options.A: Air stays locked inside each house
options.C: Atmosphere circulates freely across neighbourhoods, cities, and countries—so collective action on clean transport, green cover, and non-polluting industry is essential

explanation: Shared planetary commons like air and climate require community-wide and global stewardship.

subject: Science
question: Which core message best summarises NCERT Curiosity Chapter 11 ("Nature’s Treasures")?

options.A: Air, water, sunlight, soil, forests, rocks, minerals, and fossil fuels are precious interdependent gifts of nature—conserving renewable resources and transitioning away from finite polluting fossil fuels is vital for a sustainable future
options.B: Only gold and diamonds count as Nature’s treasures
options.C: Human technology no longer depends on nature
options.D: Natural resources are unlimited and never need conservation

explanation: Responsible stewardship of both renewable and non-renewable natural treasures protects life for generations to come.

subject: Science
question: What is a group of stars that appears to form a recognisable imaginary pattern in the night sky called?
explanation: Constellations are regions/patterns of stars in the night sky named after mythical figures, animals, or objects.

subject: Science
question: Which star is the closest star to Earth and the centre of our Solar System?
explanation: The Sun is our own star, supplying the light and heat that sustain life on Earth.

subject: Science
question: Which star in the northern night sky appears almost stationary in the north direction and has guided travellers for centuries?
explanation: Polaris lies almost directly above Earth’s North Pole axis, so it appears fixed in the north.

subject: Science
question: In Indian astronomy, what is the traditional name for the seven bright stars of the Big Dipper (part of Ursa Major)?
explanation: The seven bright stars forming a ladle/plough shape in Ursa Major are known in India as *Saptarishi*.

subject: Science
question: Which constellation is famously known as "The Hunter" and has three bright stars in a straight row forming its belt?
explanation: Orion (The Hunter) is easily recognised in winter skies by the three aligned stars of Orion’s Belt.

subject: Science
question: Which is the brightest star in the entire night sky (excluding the Sun), located in the constellation Canis Major?
explanation: Sirius (known in India as *Lubdhaka*) is the brightest star visible in Earth’s night sky.

subject: Science
question: How many official planets revolve around the Sun in our Solar System?
explanation: There are 8 planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune (Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006).

subject: Science
question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
explanation: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun.

subject: Science
question: Which planet is famously known as the "Red Planet" due to reddish iron-oxide dust on its surface?
explanation: Rust-coloured iron-rich soil gives Mars its distinctive reddish hue.

subject: Science
question: Which planet is known as the "Blue Planet" because about 70% of its surface is covered with liquid water?
explanation: Earth’s vast liquid oceans make it appear predominantly blue from space.

subject: Science
question: Which is the LARGEST planet in our Solar System?
explanation: Jupiter is the most massive and largest gas giant in the Solar System.

subject: Science
question: Which planet is famous for its bright, wide system of icy and rocky rings clearly visible through a small telescope?
explanation: Saturn’s prominent, bright ring system makes it iconic among planets.

subject: Science
question: What is Earth’s ONLY natural satellite?
explanation: The Moon orbits Earth once roughly every 27–29 days.

subject: Science
question: What is the name of our home galaxy—a vast spiral collection of billions of stars visible as a faint glowing band across a dark night sky?
explanation: Our Solar System resides inside the Milky Way Galaxy, called *Akash Ganga* in India.

subject: Science
question: Why do stars shine brightly on their own, whereas planets and the Moon are visible only because they reflect sunlight?

options.A: Stars are closer than the Moon
options.C: Stars produce their own light; planets and moons do not produce their own light

explanation: Stars generate intense light internally, while planets and satellites shine solely by reflecting starlight.

subject: Science
question: Small rocky, irregularly shaped objects orbiting the Sun—mostly concentrated in a belt between Mars and Jupiter—are called:
explanation: The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.

subject: Science
question: Icy visitors from the outer Solar System that develop a glowing coma and long tail when they approach the Sun are called:
explanation: Solar heat vaporises a comet’s surface ices into a glowing gas/dust tail.

subject: Science
question: Which historic Indian lunar mission made India the first country to soft-land near the Moon’s south pole in August 2023?
explanation: ISRO’s Chandrayaan-3 achieved a landmark soft landing near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023 (National Space Day).

subject: Science
question: Why can we see far more stars in the night sky from a quiet rural village than from the middle of a brightly lit big city?

options.A: Stars do not exist above cities
options.B: Excessive artificial city lights cause light pollution (and urban dust/smoke reduces clarity), washing out faint stars
options.D: Villages are closer to the Sun

explanation: Light pollution brightens the urban night sky, hiding dimmer stars and the Milky Way.

subject: Science
question: How can you locate the Pole Star (Polaris / *Dhruva Tara*) in the northern sky using the Big Dipper (*Saptarishi*)?

options.B: Draw an imaginary straight line through the two outer "pointer" stars at the front edge of the Big Dipper’s bowl and extend it about 5 times their distance straight to Polaris
options.C: Look toward the setting Sun only
options.D: Look directly straight down at the ground

explanation: The two pointer stars of the Big Dipper point almost directly toward Polaris.

subject: Science
question: Why is Venus often called the "Morning Star" or "Evening Star" even though it is actually a planet?

options.A: Venus shines brilliantly near the horizon just before sunrise or just after sunset, making it look like a super-bright star to the naked eye
options.C: Venus produces its own nuclear light

explanation: Thick reflective clouds make Venus the brightest planet in our sky, visible near dawn or dusk.

subject: Science
question: Even though Mercury is closest to the Sun, which planet is actually the HOTTEST planet in our Solar System?
explanation: Venus has an extremely thick carbon dioxide atmosphere that traps intense heat (runaway greenhouse effect).

subject: Science
question: Arrange the four INNER rocky planets in order of increasing distance from the Sun:
explanation: The four inner terrestrial planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.

subject: Science
question: Arrange the four OUTER giant planets in order of increasing distance from the Sun:
explanation: Beyond the asteroid belt lie the four gas/ice giants: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

subject: Science
question: Why was Pluto reclassified from a "planet" to a "dwarf planet" in 2006 by the International Astronomical Union (IAU)?

options.C: Pluto is very small and shares its orbital neighbourhood with many other icy objects instead of clearing its orbit

explanation: Under the IAU definition, a full planet must clear other comparable objects from its orbital zone; Pluto has not.

subject: Science
question: How can you use Orion’s Belt (the three stars in a straight line) to find Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky?

options.A: Extend an imaginary straight line along Orion’s three belt stars downward/eastward—it points straight toward brilliant Sirius
options.B: Look straight north to the horizon

explanation: Orion’s Belt acts as a convenient sky pointer leading directly to Sirius in Canis Major.

subject: Science
question: What causes the bowl-shaped depressions called CRATERS covering the surface of the Moon?

options.B: Impacts of asteroids and rocky space debris hitting the Moon over billions of years, preserved because the Moon has no atmosphere or weather to erode them

explanation: Without air, rain, or wind to wear them away, impact craters remain preserved for eons.

subject: Science
question: Approximately how long does the Moon take to complete one full revolution around Earth?
explanation: The Moon orbits Earth in about 27 days.

subject: Science
question: Approximately how long does Earth take to complete one full revolution around the Sun?
explanation: Earth’s orbital period around the Sun defines one year (~365.25 days).

subject: Science
question: Which famous comet returns to the inner Solar System roughly once every 76 years (last seen in 1986, next expected around 2061)?
explanation: Halley’s Comet is the best-known periodic comet visible from Earth roughly every 76 years.

subject: Science
question: What is the main physical difference between the 4 inner planets (Mercury–Mars) and the 4 outer planets (Jupiter–Neptune)?

options.A: Inner planets are smaller with solid rocky surfaces; outer planets are huge giants composed mostly of gases (and ices)
options.B: Inner planets are made of gas; outer planets are tiny rocks
options.C: Inner planets are colder than Neptune
options.D: Outer planets have no moons at all

explanation: Rocky terrestrial inner planets contrast sharply with giant gaseous outer planets.

subject: Science
question: Why do stars appear as tiny pinpoints of light in the night sky, whereas the Sun looks like a huge blazing disc?

options.A: Other stars are smaller than pebbles
options.B: The Sun is vastly closer to Earth (~150 million km), while other stars are trillions of kilometres farther away
options.C: The Sun is not a star
options.D: Other stars are dimmer than candles

explanation: Apparent size depends dramatically on distance; many distant stars are actually much larger and brighter than our Sun.

subject: Science
question: In which constellation is Polaris (the Pole Star) located?
explanation: Polaris sits at the tip of the handle of the Little Dipper (Ursa Minor).

subject: Science
question: What name was given to the landing site of India’s Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander on the Moon?
explanation: India officially named the Chandrayaan-3 landing site *Shiv Shakti Point* and declared 23 August National Space Day.

subject: Science
question: Why can we NOT see other stars during the daytime even though they are still shining up in the sky?

options.A: Stars switch off during the day
options.B: Clouds eat all stars at noon
options.C: Bright sunlight scattered across Earth’s atmosphere completely outshines the much fainter light of distant stars

explanation: Stars remain in the daytime sky, but bright blue scattered sunlight overwhelms them.

subject: Science
question: What is a "satellite" in astronomy?

options.B: A rock sitting on a mountain
options.C: Any object that revolves around a larger celestial body (such as a natural moon or a human-made spacecraft orbiting a planet)

explanation: Satellites can be natural (like the Moon) or artificial (communication/weather spacecraft).

subject: Science
question: How can a sharp-eyed stargazer tell a bright PLANET (like Jupiter or Venus) apart from a bright STAR in the night sky without a telescope?

options.D: Stars appear to twinkle noticeably, whereas planets generally shine with a steady, non-twinkling light (and slowly shift position against background stars over weeks)

explanation: Because planets are much closer and appear as tiny discs rather than single points, atmospheric turbulence does not make them twinkle like distant point-like stars.

subject: Science
question: Why is Polaris (the Pole Star) NOT visible from Australia or South Africa in the Southern Hemisphere?

options.B: Polaris sits almost directly above Earth’s North Pole, so Earth’s own curved sphere blocks it below the northern horizon for observers south of the Equator
options.D: Polaris moves to the south in winter

explanation: An observer’s latitude determines which hemisphere of the celestial sphere is visible above the horizon.

subject: Science
question: A student asks: "If the Sun is just an ordinary star, why is it measured in Astronomical Units (1 AU ≈ 150 million km) while other stars are measured in light-years?"

options.A: Other stars are closer than Mars
options.C: Kilometres do not exist outside Earth
options.D: Distances inside our Solar System are millions of kilometres (convenient in AU), whereas other stars are so immensely far away that even light takes years to reach us

explanation: Astronomers choose distance units matched to the vast scale of planetary vs interstellar space.

subject: Science
question: Why does Earth support abundant liquid water and life, whereas Venus is scorching hot (~460 °C) and Mars is freezing cold?

options.B: Earth orbits in the Sun’s habitable "Goldilocks" zone at just the right distance and has a balanced atmosphere that keeps temperatures suitable for liquid water
options.D: Venus is farther from the Sun than Neptune

explanation: Optimal distance from the Sun combined with a protective atmosphere maintains Earth’s life-friendly climate.

subject: Science
question: What is the purpose of India’s *Aditya-L1* space mission (launched by ISRO in 2023)?

options.B: To study the Sun and solar weather from a stable vantage point in space

explanation: Aditya-L1 is India’s first dedicated space-based solar observatory.

subject: Science
question: Why do astronauts on the Moon have to wear bulky pressurised spacesuits and communicate via radio instead of talking directly through the air?

options.A: The Moon is covered in liquid ocean
options.B: Spacesuits make them heavier than Jupiter
options.C: The Moon has virtually no atmosphere—so there is no breathable oxygen, extreme temperature swings, and no air medium for sound waves to travel
options.D: Sound travels too fast on the Moon

explanation: Absence of a lunar atmosphere means zero breathable air and zero acoustic transmission.

subject: Science
question: Which statement about the Asteroid Belt is scientifically CORRECT?

options.B: It lies between Mercury and Venus
options.C: It is a solid brick wall around Earth
options.D: It is a vast region between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter containing thousands of rocky asteroids orbiting the Sun, with huge empty spaces between them

explanation: Asteroids are widely spaced rocky remnants from the early Solar System orbiting mainly between Mars and Jupiter.

subject: Science
question: Why do we see different constellations in the winter night sky (like Orion) than in the summer night sky?

options.C: As Earth revolves around the Sun over the year, Earth’s nighttime side faces different directions out into space

explanation: Earth’s annual orbit shifts which region of the celestial sphere lies opposite the Sun at night.

subject: Science
question: Which planet has the MOST extreme rings visible from Earth, yet ALL FOUR outer giant planets actually possess ring systems?

options.D: Saturn has the brightest, most prominent rings; Jupiter, Uranus, and Neptune also have fainter rings

explanation: While Saturn’s rings are spectacularly bright, space probes discovered fainter rings around Jupiter, Uranus, and Neptune too.

subject: Science
question: Why do astronomers build major observatories (like the Indian Astronomical Observatory at Hanle, Ladakh) on high, dry, remote mountains?

options.A: High altitude means thinner, drier air with less cloud cover, and remoteness ensures minimal light pollution for crystal-clear stargazing
options.C: Mountains are half the distance to the Moon

explanation: Clear, dry, dark skies at high elevation dramatically sharpen astronomical observations.

subject: Science
question: If you watch the Big Dipper (*Saptarishi*) over 4 hours on a clear night, it appears to slowly wheel counter-clockwise around the Pole Star. What causes this apparent rotation of the night sky?

options.A: The Moon pulling stars in a circle
options.B: The Pole Star pushing other stars
options.D: Earth’s rotation on its axis from west to east

explanation: Earth’s daily spin makes the sky appear to rotate around the celestial pole (Polaris).

subject: Science
question: Which planet rotates on its side (with an extreme axial tilt) and appears pale cyan-blue?
explanation: Uranus is an ice giant tilted almost sideways relative to its orbit.

subject: Science
question: How are artificial satellites useful in everyday life across India?

options.B: They enable weather forecasting, cyclone warnings, GPS navigation, television/internet communication, and mapping of crops and forests
options.C: They block sunlight to cool summer

explanation: Space technology directly supports disaster management, agriculture, navigation, and communication.

subject: Science
question: What happens to a comet’s tail as the comet swings close to the Sun?

options.A: The tail always trails straight behind its motion like smoke
options.B: The comet turns into a planet
options.C: The tail freezes solid near the Sun
options.D: Solar radiation and solar wind blow vaporised gas and dust into a glowing tail that always points AWAY from the Sun

explanation: Because solar wind pushes the vapour outward, a comet’s tail points away from the Sun even when the comet is moving outward.

subject: Science
question: Why do we NOT feel dizzy or get thrown off even though Earth is spinning on its axis and revolving rapidly around the Sun?

options.B: Everything around us—the ground, oceans, air, and our bodies—moves smoothly together at a constant steady speed, and Earth’s gravity holds us firmly down
options.C: Air glues our shoes to rocks

explanation: Smooth, uniform motion shared by the observer and surroundings is imperceptible without external reference shifts.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following is the LARGEST astronomical structure in scale, arranged from smallest to largest?

options.A: Solar System < Earth < Milky Way < Moon
options.C: Universe < Galaxy < Solar System < Earth < Moon
options.D: Moon < Earth < Solar System < Milky Way Galaxy < Universe

explanation: Our Moon orbits Earth, inside our Solar System, which is one of billions of star systems in the Milky Way Galaxy, inside the vast Universe.

subject: Science
question: Why does Mars take nearly TWO Earth years (687 Earth days) to complete one orbit around the Sun, while Mercury takes only 88 Earth days?

options.A: Planets farther from the Sun travel along much larger orbital paths and move more slowly under weaker solar gravity

explanation: Orbital period increases dramatically with distance from the Sun.

subject: Science
question: What are planets discovered orbiting OTHER distant stars outside our own Solar System called?
explanation: Thousands of exoplanets have been discovered orbiting other stars in the Milky Way.

subject: Science
question:
Assertion (A): Even though the stars in a constellation like Orion appear close together as a flat pattern in our night sky, they are actually at vastly different distances from Earth in 3D space.
Reason (R): From Earth, we only see the two-dimensional direction of stars along our line of sight, not their true depth in space.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

explanation: Constellation stars are line-of-sight alignments; viewing them from another star system would completely scramble the pattern.

subject: Science
question:
Assertion (A): Venus is hotter than Mercury even though Mercury is much closer to the Sun.
Reason (R): Venus is wrapped in an extremely dense carbon-dioxide atmosphere that traps solar heat intensely, whereas Mercury has practically no atmosphere to retain heat.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

explanation: Venus’s runaway greenhouse effect raises its surface temperature above 460 °C day and night.

subject: Science
question: Case Study: A student in Delhi (latitude ~28° N) looks north on a clear night and sees Polaris about 28° above the northern horizon. If she travels north to Leh (latitude ~34° N), where will Polaris appear?

options.D: Higher in the northern sky—about 34° above the northern horizon (the altitude of Polaris roughly equals the observer’s northern latitude)

explanation: In the Northern Hemisphere, Polaris’s elevation angle above the northern horizon equals the observer’s latitude—a key tool of celestial navigation.

subject: Science
question: Why does light from the Sun take about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, whereas light from the Moon reaches Earth in just ~1.3 seconds?

options.C: The Sun (~150 million km) is nearly 400 times farther from Earth than the Moon (~384,000 km), and light travels at a finite constant speed (~300,000 km/s)

explanation: At ~300,000 km/s, 384,000 km takes ~1.3 s while 150,000,000 km takes ~500 s (8 min 20 s).

subject: Science
question: A student looks at the Moon through binoculars and sees dark flat plains and bright rugged cratered highlands. Why did ISRO specifically target the Moon’s SOUTH POLE region for Chandrayaan-3?

options.A: The south pole is covered in forests
options.B: The south pole is closer to Mars
options.C: Permanently shadowed craters near the lunar south pole are believed to hold valuable water-ice deposits and pristine scientific clues about the early Solar System
options.D: There are no craters at the south pole

explanation: Lunar polar water ice could support future human space exploration and scientific study.

subject: Science
question: Why do astronomers say that looking at a star 100 light-years away is like looking 100 years BACK IN TIME?

options.D: Light emitted by that star took 100 years to travel across space to reach our eyes, so we see the star as it looked 100 years ago

explanation: Finite light speed means observing distant cosmic objects always reveals their past state.

subject: Science
question: How does reducing unnecessary upward-pointing outdoor streetlights (using shielded downward-facing fixtures) help BOTH astronomy AND energy conservation?

options.B: Shielded lamps turn off roads completely
options.C: Shielded lamps direct light strictly onto roads where needed—cutting wasted electricity AND reducing skyglow/light pollution so night skies remain dark

explanation: Smart lighting design saves electricity, protects nocturnal wildlife, and restores starry skies.

subject: Science
question: Compare the Earth’s Moon with Jupiter’s moons (like Europa and Ganymede): why do outer gas giants like Jupiter and Saturn have DOZENS of moons while Mercury and Venus have ZERO?

options.A: Jupiter is closer to the Sun
options.B: Only icy planets can have gravity
options.C: Mercury destroyed its moons with rain
options.D: Giant outer planets have far stronger gravitational pull and formed farther from the Sun’s intense gravitational tug, allowing them to hold and capture many moons

explanation: Massive gravity and wider Hill spheres far from the Sun allow giant planets to retain large moon systems.

subject: Science
question: A student observes the Moon on a Full Moon night and notices it rises around sunset in the east. Where is the Sun relative to Earth and the Moon at Full Moon?

options.A: The Moon produces its own light on Full Moon night
options.B: Earth lies roughly between the Sun and the Moon, so sunlight illuminates the entire Earth-facing side of the Moon
options.C: The Moon lies directly between Earth and the Sun
options.D: The Sun is behind the Moon

explanation: Full Moon occurs when the Moon is opposite the Sun in Earth’s sky.

subject: Science
question: Why do we NOT experience a solar eclipse every New Moon or a lunar eclipse every Full Moon?

options.A: The Moon stops orbiting every other month
options.B: The Moon’s orbital path around Earth is slightly tilted (~5°) relative to Earth’s orbit around the Sun, so most months the Moon passes slightly above or below the exact alignment line
options.D: Clouds hide eclipses 11 months a year

explanation: Eclipses occur only when New or Full Moon happens near the orbital intersection points (nodes).

subject: Science
question: Why does a meteor ("shooting star") flash brightly across the night sky for a second and vanish, even though it is NOT actually a star?

options.A: A real star fell onto a mountain
options.B: It is a piece of the Moon falling
options.C: It is an airplane turning off its lights
options.D: It is a tiny grain of space dust or rock entering Earth’s atmosphere at tremendous speed, heating up and glowing brightly from atmospheric friction

explanation: Meteors are tiny meteoroids vaporising high in Earth’s atmosphere—unrelated to distant stars.

subject: Science
question: Which planet has a day (one rotation on its axis) LONGER than its year (one revolution around the Sun) and rotates backward (east to west)?
explanation: Venus spins very slowly in retrograde (clockwise) direction—taking ~243 Earth days to rotate vs ~225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.

subject: Science
question: Why is Jupiter—the largest planet—also the FASTEST spinning planet in the Solar System, completing one rotation in less than 10 hours?

options.C: Rapid rotation is preserved from the swirling gas cloud from which Jupiter formed, creating its prominent banded cloud stripes and slight equatorial bulge

explanation: Conservation of angular momentum from Solar System formation gave giant Jupiter a ~9.9-hour day.

subject: Science
question: A sky-watching app shows a bright object moving slowly night after night relative to the fixed stars of Orion. What must this object be?

options.A: A planet (or possibly an asteroid/comet) within our Solar System

explanation: The word "planet" comes from the Greek for "wanderer" because planets visibly drift across the fixed background constellations.

subject: Science
question: Why do Indian traditional calendars and festivals often track both lunar phases (Full Moon / *Purnima*, New Moon / *Amavasya*) and solar cycles?

options.B: Only the Moon is visible in India
options.C: Observing the regular, predictable cycles of the Moon’s phases and the Sun’s annual path gave ancient societies accurate timekeeping for seasons and agriculture

explanation: Astronomical cycles formed the basis of human timekeeping and agricultural calendars worldwide.

subject: Science
question: If a spacecraft travels at 10 km/s straight toward the Moon (~384,000 km away), roughly how many hours would the straight-line journey take?
explanation: Time = 384,000 km ÷ 10 km/s = 38,400 seconds ÷ 3,600 s/hr ≈ 10.67 hours (real missions use curved fuel-saving orbits taking ~3–40 days).

subject: Science
question: Why is it dangerous to look DIRECTLY at the Sun—even during a partial solar eclipse—without certified solar-viewing filters?

options.C: Eclipses make the Sun emit magnets
options.D: Intense visible and invisible ultraviolet/infrared radiation from the Sun can permanently burn the retina of the eye within seconds

explanation: Direct solar viewing without ISO-certified solar filters risks permanent eye damage.

subject: Science
question: Which pair correctly links an Indian space milestone with its target?

options.A: Mangalyaan → Saturn; Aditya-L1 → Moon; Chandrayaan-3 → Venus
options.D: Mangalyaan (MOM) → Mars; Chandrayaan-3 → Moon; Aditya-L1 → Sun

explanation: ISRO’s landmark missions span Mars (Mangalyaan), the Moon (Chandrayaan series), and the Sun (Aditya-L1).

subject: Science
question: Case Study: Two students observe the night sky on 15 December at 9 PM: Student A is in a dark village in Ladakh (Hanle Dark Sky Reserve) and Student B is in a brightly lit commercial street in Mumbai. Student A sees the faint glowing band of the Milky Way (*Akash Ganga*) and over 2,000 stars; Student B sees barely 30 bright stars and Jupiter. Which factor explains this huge difference?

options.A: The Milky Way is only above Ladakh
options.C: Severe urban light pollution and atmospheric haze in Mumbai wash out faint celestial objects, whereas high, dry, dark skies in Hanle preserve natural night-sky visibility
options.D: Mumbai is closer to the Sun

explanation: Hanle is India’s first official Dark Sky Reserve, specifically protected against artificial light pollution.

subject: Science
question: Why does the Moon appear almost the EXACT same angular size in Earth’s sky as the Sun—making dramatic total solar eclipses possible—even though the Sun’s diameter is about 400 times larger than the Moon’s?

options.A: By a remarkable cosmic coincidence, the Sun is also about 400 times FARTHER away from Earth than the Moon, so their apparent sizes in our sky closely match
options.B: The Sun shrinks to Moon-size once a year

explanation: Ratio of diameter (~400:1) cancels ratio of distance (~400:1), giving both ~0.5° apparent angular diameter.

subject: Science
question: A student builds a scale model of the Solar System where the Sun is a large 1-metre-wide beach ball. On this exact scale, Earth would be roughly the size of a tiny 1 cm marble placed about 107 metres away (a whole football field away!). What big lesson does this scale model teach?

options.A: Space is overwhelmingly vast and mostly empty—textbook diagrams compress distances dramatically so all planets can fit on one page
options.B: Planets actually touch each other in space
options.C: Earth is bigger than the Sun
options.D: The Moon is farther than Jupiter

explanation: True-to-scale models correct the common textbook misconception that planets sit tightly packed together.

subject: Science
question:
Assertion (A): A comet’s glowing tail points AWAY from the Sun both while approaching the Sun AND while moving away from the Sun.
Reason (R): The tail is pushed outward by solar radiation pressure and the stream of charged particles (solar wind) blowing radially out from the Sun.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

explanation: Because solar wind blows outward from the Sun, when a comet departs the inner Solar System its tail actually leads ahead of it!

subject: Science
question: If Earth’s rotation on its axis suddenly reversed (spinning east to west instead of west to east), where would the Sun rise and set?

options.A: There would be no sunrise or sunset
options.B: The Sun would rise in the North
options.D: The Sun would rise in the WEST and set in the EAST

explanation: Apparent east-to-west motion of the Sun is directly caused by Earth’s west-to-east spin (just as on retrograde-spinning Venus, the Sun rises in the west).

subject: Science
question: Why do astronomers search specifically for rocky exoplanets orbiting within a star’s "habitable zone" when looking for potential life beyond Earth?

options.A: Stars exist only inside habitable zones
options.B: In the habitable zone, a rocky planet receives the right range of stellar warmth for liquid water—essential for life as we know it—to exist on its surface
options.C: Only planets in the habitable zone have gravity

explanation: Surface liquid water is the primary benchmark guiding the scientific search for habitable exoplanets.

subject: Science
question: Why did ancient Indian navigators and travellers across the Arabian Sea and Himalayan trade routes rely so heavily on *Dhruva Tara* (Polaris) at night?

options.A: Magnetic compasses cannot point north on ships
options.B: Unlike the Sun or Moon which move across the sky, Polaris stays virtually fixed due north all night and all year, giving an instant compass direction and approximate latitude
options.C: Polaris is brighter than the Sun

question: प्रकरण अध्ययन: स्कूल के बगीचे में किसी ने नए पौधे उखाड़ दिए। प्रिंसिपल के पास दो छात्रों को बिना प्रमाण पकड़ा गया। ‘तीन बुद्धिमान’ की सीख से कक्षा-कप्तान जांच कैसे करेगा?

options.D: बगीचे की गीली मिट्टी में जूतों के निशान, समय, और गिरी पत्तियों जैसे तथ्यों का शांत अवलोकन करके सच परखेगा

explanation: सत्यनिष्ठ अवलोकन निर्दोष को बचाता और सही कारण खोजता है।

subject: Hindi
question: प्रकरण अध्ययन: लोककथाएं पीढ़ी-दर-पीढ़ी मौखिक रूप से क्यों जीवित रहती हैं? ‘तीन बुद्धिमान’ के संदर्भ में प्रमुख कारण क्या है?

options.A: सरल, रोचक घटनाक्रम के भीतर जीवन की गहरी व्यावहारिक सूझबूझ और मनोरंजक कौतूहल छिपा होता है
options.B: इनमें कठिन संस्कृत व्याकरण होता है
options.C: इन्हें केवल राजाओं के दरबार में गाया जाता है

explanation: लोक-बुद्धि और कथानक का कौतूहल इन्हें सदाबहार बनाते हैं।

subject: Hindi
question: “फूल और काँटा” कविता के प्रसिद्ध कवि कौन हैं?
explanation: ‘हरिऔध’ जी की यह नीतिपरक कविता जन्म की अपेक्षा कर्म व आचरण की महानता सिद्ध करती है।

subject: Hindi
question: कविता के अनुसार फूल और काँटा किस समान स्थान पर जन्म लेते हैं?

options.C: एक ही पौधे की डाल पर एक साथ

explanation: “हैं जन्म लेते जगह में एक ही, एक ही पौधा उन्हें है पालता” — परिवेश और पालन-पोषण दोनों का समान है।

subject: Hindi
question: रात में उन दोनों (फूल और काँटे) पर समान रूप से चाँदनी और वर्षा किस प्रकार बरसती है?

options.A: काँटे पर सिर्फ अंधेरा रहता है
options.B: हवा सिर्फ फूल को छूती है
options.C: फूल को कम पानी मिलता है
options.D: दोनों पर चंद्रमा की उज्ज्वल किरणें और मेघ समान रूप से जल बरसाते हैं

explanation: प्रकृति दोनों का पोषण बिना किसी भेदभाव के समान रूप से करती है।

subject: Hindi
question: परिवेश एक होने के बावजूद काँटा अपने स्वभाव से क्या कष्टकारी व्यवहार करता है?

options.C: किसी की उँगलियाँ छेद देता है और तितलियों के सुंदर कोमल पंख फाड़ देता है

explanation: कठोर और स्वार्थी आचरण के कारण काँटा दूसरों को पीड़ा पहुँचाता है।

subject: Hindi
question: इसके विपरीत, फूल अपने मधुर स्वभाव से किन-किन जीवों और लोगों को आनंद प्रदान करता है?

options.A: केवल रात में छिप जाता है
options.D: भौंरों को अनूठा रस पिलाता है, तितलियों को गोद में लेता है और अपनी सुगंध से सबका मन मोह लेता है

explanation: फूल सौंदर्य, सुगंध और परोपकार के गुणों से सबका प्रिय बनता है।

subject: Hindi
question: अपनी सद्वृत्ति और गुणों के कारण फूल को अंततः कौन-सा सर्वोच्च सम्मान प्राप्त होता है?

options.C: सबकी आँखों में बसकर वह देवताओं के शीश (मस्तक) पर आदर सहित चढ़ाया जाता है

explanation: “सदा रहता है सबों को ही खला” काँटे के विपरीत, फूल देवताओं के मुकुट व शीश का शृंगार बनता है।

subject: Hindi
question: पूरी कविता का केंद्रीय संदेश क्या है?

options.B: व्यक्ति जन्म या कुल से नहीं, बल्कि अपने सद्गुणों और कर्मों से महान अथवा निंदनीय बनता है
options.D: अमीर परिवार में पैदा होना ही सबसे बड़ा है

explanation: “किस तरह कुल की बड़ाई काम दे, जो किसी में हो बड़प्पन की कसर” — कर्म और चरित्र ही कसौटी हैं।

subject: Hindi
question: कविता में प्रयुक्त ‘मेह’ और ‘बसन’ शब्दों के क्रमशः सही अर्थ क्या हैं?
explanation: “मेह उन पर है बरसता एक सा” (वर्षा) तथा “फाड़ देता है किसी का वर बसन” (सुंदर वस्त्र)।

subject: Hindi
question: “जो किसी में हो बड़प्पन की कसर” में ‘बड़प्पन की कसर’ का क्या आशय है?

options.C: चरित्र, उदारता, और सद्गुणों की कमी होना

explanation: ऊँचे कुल का नाम भी तब काम नहीं आता यदि व्यक्ति में आंतरिक बड़प्पन (सद्व्यवहार) न हो।

subject: Hindi
question: हरिऔध जी ने प्राकृतिक प्रतीकों (फूल और काँटा) को मानव समाज पर लागू करके कौन-सा भाव स्पष्ट किया?

options.A: तितलियाँ केवल रात में उड़ती हैं
options.B: समान अवसर मिलने पर भी अलग-अलग व्यक्ति अपने चयन और आचरण से भिन्न चरित्र निर्मित करते हैं

explanation: प्रकृति का रूपक समान परिस्थितियों में व्यक्तिगत कर्म-चयन की ज़िम्मेदारी दिखाता है।

subject: Hindi
question: ‘खटकता एक सबकी आँख में’ मुहावरे का उचित अर्थ है:

options.D: अपने बुरे व्यवहार के कारण सबको अप्रिय और चुभने वाला लगना

explanation: ‘आँख में खटकना’ किसी की अप्रिय उपस्थिति या द्वेष को दर्शाता है।

subject: Hindi
question: ‘सुगंध’ शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग लगा है और उसका विलोम क्या होगा?
explanation: ‘सु’ (अच्छा) के विपरीत ‘दुर्’ (बुरा) उपसर्ग लगकर ‘दुर्गंध’ बनता है।

subject: Hindi
question: एक ही विद्यालय, एक ही कक्षा और समान शिक्षकों से पढ़ने वाले दो छात्रों में यदि एक विनम्र-सहायक बने और दूसरा अहंकारी-चिड़चिड़ा, तो इस स्थिति की तुलना कविता के किस अंश से सबसे सटीक होगी?

options.C: समान पौधे, समान हवा-पानी पाकर भी फूल और काँटे के विपरीत स्वभाव विकसित होने से

explanation: यह कविता समकालीन छात्र जीवन और चरित्र निर्माण से सीधे जुड़ती है।

subject: Hindi
question: “डाल पर खिलते हुए भी फूल की नम्रता और सुगंध उसे ईश्वर के चरणों तक ले जाती है” — इसमें कौन-सा जीवन मूल्य निहित है?
explanation: दूसरों को सुख देने वाला जीवन स्वतः आदर का पात्र बनता है।

subject: Hindi
question: संयुक्त क्रिया पहचानिए: “काँटा तितलियों के पंख फाड़ देता है।”
explanation: दो क्रियाओं के योग से पूर्ण अर्थ देने पर संयुक्त क्रिया बनती है।

subject: Hindi
question: निम्न में से ‘भौंरा’ शब्द का तत्सम शुद्ध रूप कौन-सा है?
explanation: संस्कृत तत्सम शब्द ‘भ्रमर’ तद्भव में भौंरा बन जाता है।

subject: Hindi
question: कथन (A): जन्मजात ऊँचा कुल या बड़े नाम का सहारा बुरे कर्मों को सम्माननीय नहीं बना सकता। कारण (R): समाज और समय किसी व्यक्ति का मूल्यांकन उसके आचरण, विनम्रता और दूसरों के प्रति व्यवहार के आधार पर ही करते हैं।

options.A: A और R दोनों सत्य हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या करता है
options.B: A और R दोनों सत्य हैं, पर R सही व्याख्या नहीं है
options.C: A सत्य है, R असत्य है
options.D: A असत्य है, R सत्य है

explanation: कविता की अंतिम पंक्तियाँ कर्म-प्रधान समाजशास्त्र को स्वर देती हैं।

subject: Hindi
question: कथन (A): काँटे के चुभने के लिए बाहरी मौसम और पौधे की जड़ें ही पूर्णतः दोषी थीं। कारण (R): समान वर्षा, धूप और हवा मिलने पर भी फूल ने मधुर रस और सुगंध पैदा की।

options.A: A और R दोनों सत्य हैं
options.B: A सत्य है, R असत्य है
options.C: A असत्य है, R सत्य है
options.D: A और R दोनों असत्य हैं

explanation: समान पोषण रहते दोष बाहर नहीं, स्वयं के आचरण में था।

subject: Hindi
question: प्रकरण अध्ययन: एक छात्र कक्षा में कमज़ोर सहपाठियों की कॉपी फाड़ता व मज़ाक उड़ाता है जबकि उसी बैंच का दूसरा छात्र नोट्स बाँटकर सबकी मदद करता है। ‘फूल और काँटा’ पाठ पर आधारित चर्चा में शिक्षक क्या निष्कर्ष निकालेंगे?

options.A: समान कक्षा मिलने पर भी हमारा व्यवहार तय करता है कि हम दूसरों को चुभने वाले काँटे बनेंगे या सबका मन मोहने वाले फूल!
options.C: दोनों को कक्षा से निकाल दें

explanation: काव्य पाठ को दैनिक कक्षा संस्कृति में ढालना नैतिक शिक्षा को जीवंत बनाता है।

subject: Hindi
question: प्रकरण अध्ययन: ‘फूल और काँटा’ को स्वर-लहरी में गाकर याद करने से क्या लाभ होता है?

options.B: तुकबंदी और लयात्मकता से खड़ीबोली हिंदी के सुंदर शब्द और नैतिक सूत्र वर्षों तक कंठस्थ रहते हैं

explanation: छंदबद्ध लय साहित्यिक संवेदनशीलता और स्मृति दोनों निखारती है।

subject: Hindi
question: “पानी रे पानी” प्रसिद्ध पर्यावरण-निबंध के लेखक कौन हैं?
explanation: गाँधीवादी पर्यावरणविद् एवं जल-संरक्षण विचारक अनुपम मिश्र ने जल-चक्र और परंपरागत जल प्रबंधन पर यह सरल मार्मिक निबंध लिखा है।

subject: Hindi
question: लेखक के अनुसार जल-चक्र (Water Cycle) को हम सामान्यतः कहाँ पढ़ते हैं और असली जीवन में उसे कब महसूस करते हैं?

options.D: भूगोल की किताबों में जल-चक्र के सुंदर चित्र पढ़ते हैं, और जब नल सूखते या गलियाँ डूबती हैं तब उसकी वास्तविक कीमत समझ आती है

explanation: किताबी ज्ञान और रोज़मर्रा के नल-अकाल/बाढ़ का सीधा संबंध लेख में उजागर हुआ है।

subject: Hindi
question: हमारा देश भारत किस बड़ी मौसमी वर्षा-प्रणाली पर जल आपूर्ति के लिए निर्भर रहता है?

options.A: मानसून (जून–सितंबर के तीन–चार महीनों की वर्षा) पर

explanation: पूरे वर्ष की नदियाँ, झीलें और भूजल मुख्यतः कुछ महीनों की मानसूनी बारिश से ही भरते हैं।

subject: Hindi
question: एक समय में शहर-गाँव के तालाब, जोहड़ और पोखर वर्षा का पानी सँभालकर किस रूप में काम आते थे?

options.A: प्रचुर बरसात के पानी को रोककर धरती के भीतर (भूजल बैंक में) सुरक्षित रखने वाले जीवित जल-भंडारों के रूप में
options.B: सड़क बनाने के लिए पत्थर बनकर
options.C: केवल कचरा फेंकने के गड्ढे के रूप में

explanation: पारंपरिक तालाब बाढ़ रोकते थे और गर्मियों में कुओं को जीवित रखते थे।

subject: Hindi
question: आधुनिक शहरों में अकाल (जल-संकट) और बाढ़ दोनों एक ही शहर में साथ-साथ क्यों दिखने लगे हैं?

options.A: नल के पाइप छोटे हो गए हैं
options.B: हमने पुराने तालाबों को पाटकर उन पर घर-बाज़ार खड़े कर लिए—जिससे बारिश होते ही पानी बहकर गलियों में बाढ़ लाता है और फिर भूजल में न उतरने से गर्मियों में अकाल पड़ता है!

explanation: तालाबों के विनाश से ‘बाढ़ और सूखे’ की दोहरी समस्या जन्म लेती है—यही लेख की मुख्य चेतावनी है।

subject: Hindi
question: लेखक ने ‘पानी की गुल्लक’ (बचत बैंक) किसे कहा है?

options.A: हमारी धरती और प्राचीन तालाबों को, जिनमें बारिश की बूँद-बूँद जमा होकर पूरे साल काम आती है
options.D: रसोई के मिट्टी के घड़े को

explanation: जैसे गुल्लक में सिक्के जोड़कर कठिन वक्त में निकालते हैं, वैसे तालाब-धरती में वर्षा-जल की बचत होती है।

subject: Hindi
question: ‘बाढ़’ और ‘सुखाड़/अकाल’ की तुलना लेखक ने एक ही सिक्के के किन दो पहलुओं से की है?

options.D: जल-प्रबंधन की अनदेखी के दो विपरीत परिणाम—एक ओर बेकाबू पानी तबाही मचाता है और कुछ महीनों बाद पानी की एक बूँद को तरसना पड़ता है

explanation: समुचित जल-संग्रहण न होने पर अतिवृष्टि भी साल भर की प्यास नहीं बुझा पाती।

subject: Hindi
question: निम्नलिखित में से ‘अमूल्य’ शब्द का सही अर्थ चुनिए:

options.D: जिसका मूल्य आँका न जा सके (अत्यंत कीमती)

explanation: ‘अ + मूल्य’ अर्थात जीवनदायी जल का कोई मोल नहीं लगाया जा सकता।

subject: Hindi
question: अनुपम मिश्र ने पूरे निबंध में कठिन तकनीकी शब्दावली के बदले सरल बोलचाल की भाषा (‘गुल्लक’, ‘अकाल’, ‘खेल’) क्यों चुनी?

subject: Hindi
question: गिरिधर कविराय के प्रसिद्ध छंद “बिना विचारे जो करे, सो पाछे पछताय” में किस आदत से बचने की चेतावनी दी गई है?

subject: Hindi
question: “लाठी में गुण बहुत हैं, सदा राखिए संग” — इस प्रसिद्ध कुंडली में ‘लाठी’ प्रतीकात्मक रूप से किसकी उपयोगिता बताती है?

subject: Hindi

question: प्रकरण अध्ययन: कोई छात्र सोशल मीडिया पर बिना सत्य जाँचे एक भ्रामक संदेश गुस्से में आगे भेज देता है और बाद में विवाद बढ़ने पर शर्मिंदा होता है। गिरिधर कविराय की कौन-सी कुंडली उसे सबसे सटीक आईना दिखाती है?

question: ‘जुगलबंदी’ शब्द का सटीक अर्थ चुनिए:

options.B: दो कलाकारों (जैसे तबला वादक और नर्तक या दो गायकों) द्वारा ताल-सुर में परस्पर संवादपूर्ण व संतुलित प्रस्तुति

subject: Hindi
question: बिरजू महाराज की जीवन-कथा गणित, खेल या विज्ञान पढ़ने वाले किसी विद्यार्थी को भी कैसे प्रेरित करती है?

options.A: जैसे उत्कृष्ट कथक के लिए रोज़ाना रियाज़, बारीक ध्यान और धैर्य चाहिए, वैसे ही हर विषय में दक्षता निरंतर अभ्यास और लगन से ही आती है!
options.B: उसे भी घुँघरू पहनकर परीक्षा देनी चाहिए
options.C: संगीत के अलावा सब बेकार है
options.D: परीक्षा में केवल नृत्य आता है

explanation: साधना और रियाज़ का नियम हर क्षेत्र की श्रेष्ठता में समान लागू होता है।

subject: Hindi
question: “कथक” शब्द की व्युत्पत्ति किस धातु/शब्द से मानी जाती है?

options.A: ‘कथा’ से (अर्थात नृत्य और भाव-अभिनय द्वारा कथा कहना)

subject: Hindi
question: निम्नलिखित में से ‘सशक्त’ एवं ‘साधना’ शब्दों के क्रमशः सही अर्थ चुनिए:

options.A: मजबूत/प्रभावशाली और किसी लक्ष्य की प्राप्ति हेतु तन्मय निष्ठापूर्ण प्रयास

subject: Hindi
question: विराम चिह्नों की दृष्टि से साक्षात्कार के संवाद का शुद्ध रूप पहचानिए:

options.A: प्रश्न: बिरजू महाराज जी, आप रोज़ कितने घंटे अभ्यास करते थे?

options.C: प्रश्न; बिरजू महाराज जी! आप रोज कितने घंटे अभ्यास करते थे,
options.D: प्रश्न बिरजू महाराज जी आप रोज कितने घंटे अभ्यास करते थे

explanation: वक्ता नाम के बाद कोलन (:), संबोधन के बाद अल्पविराम (,) और प्रश्न के अंत में प्रश्नवाचक चिह्न (?) आवश्यक है।

subject: Hindi
question: कथन (A): जन्मजात प्रतिभा होने के बाद भी गुरु का मार्गदर्शन और वर्षों का रियाज़ अनिवार्य रहता है। कारण (R): बिना नियमित साधना और अनुशासन के स्वाभाविक कौशल भी निखर कर स्थायी कला नहीं बन पाता।

options.A: A और R दोनों सत्य हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या करता है
options.B: A और R दोनों सत्य हैं, पर R सही व्याख्या नहीं है
options.C: A सत्य है, R असत्य है
options.D: A असत्य है, R सत्य है
